data.gender_notes: Pandey is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘panda’, meaning servant or attendant. The name Pandey is often given to those who are believed to serve God or the divine. The name Pandey carries the meaning “Servant of God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Pandey usually hope their child will grow to embody servant of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Pandey belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pandey total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The surname Pandey became prominent during the British rule in India, when it was the most common eccentric Indian surname used by translators, teachers, and men of letters who written in Hindi or Urdu and familiar with Sanskrit, among other Indians.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Pandey carries a strong spiritual significance in Hindu culture. The name is a reminder of the role of service to the divine. It signifies a deep connection to spiritual traditions and values. Pandey is also a symbol of the devoted servant of God or the Guru. The name is a constant reminder to remain humble and selfless in one's actions and deeds.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Pandey is derived from the Sanskrit word 'pandava', meaning 'having all weapons' or 'having all knowledge'. It is a name of respect and honor, symbolizing strength, wisdom, and the ability to overcome obstacles.

historical_references.reference: The Pandey family is an influential and ancient Rajput clan of India, who trace their origin to the legendary Rajput king Raja Bhoj. The Pandey Rajputs were traditionally the rulers of the region now known as Bundelkhand in central India. They are mentioned in medieval chronicles and oral traditions.

During the Indian independence movement, several prominent figures associated with the Indian National Congress were named Pandey. Notable among them were Hriday Nath Kunzru Pandey, a lawyer and politician from Allahabad, and Ram Manohar Lohia, a socialist and leftist leader from Uttar Pradesh. These Pandey leaders were active in the freedom struggle against the British Raj in the early 20th century.

modern_usage.modern_context: The surname 'Pandey' is of Indian origin and translates to 'scholar' or 'priest'. However, in modern times, it has been associated with the Indian diaspora, particularly in business and entrepreneurship contexts. On LinkedIn, 'Pandey' is a common last name among professionals of Indian origin. On Facebook and Twitter, you may find individuals with the name 'Pandey' sharing business news and articles, promoting their startups, or engaging in discussions related to entrepreneurship and technology.
